name: Davco Jetcrete
paste:
DAVCO® JETCRETE: SPECIFICATION CLAUSE SET

Source: Davco® Jetcrete, May 2026, Version 01.01 (https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/e/davco-jetcrete.pdf)
Draft for specifier review. Wording, values and standards are quoted from that data sheet; where it is silent the clause says 'Refer to manufacturer.' Confirm the current edition before issue.

1 SCOPE
1.1 Work included. Provide Davco® Jetcrete where documented, installed or applied in accordance with this clause and the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (May 2026, Version 01.01).
1.2 Product description. Davco® Jetcrete is a dry mixed mortar for rapid repair of concrete damaged by natural wear and aggressive environments.
1.3 Intended uses stated by the manufacturer.
    - Davco® Jetcrete is a pre-blended, rapid-setting repair mortar designed for the fast repair of concrete damaged by wear, impact, and aggressive environmental conditions. It is specifically formulated for demanding applications requiring high early strength, rapid return to service, and heat-resistant concrete repairs.
    - Davco® Jetcrete is suitable for a wide range of applications, including rapid concrete and mortar repairs, anchoring of bolts and fixings, and installation of bathroom fixtures such as toilet bowls and pipe fittings. Its fast-setting properties make it ideal for situations where rapid repair and minimal downtime are essential.
1.4 Limits of use. Observe the manufacturer's limitations stated in clause 4.5.

2 MATERIALS
2.1 Product. Davco® Jetcrete
    - Product type as printed on the data sheet: 5 minute flash setting mortar
    - Supplier as printed on the data sheet: Sika Australia Pty Limited, ABN 12 001 342 329, aus.sika.com, Tel: 1300 22 33 48
2.2 Approvals, certificates and standards stated by the manufacturer. Refer to manufacturer. The data sheet reviewed (May 2026, Version 01.01) has no approvals, certificates or standards section.
2.3 Standards and test methods cited in the data sheet. Cited as written in the data sheet. A citation is not a statement that the product complies with it; conformity is stated only where the data sheet says so (see the approvals clause and the statements quoted in the other clauses).
    - AS 1478.2:2005: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Product Information > Compressive strength (p.1).
    - AS/NZS 2350.4-2006: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Application Information > Final set time (p.2); Application Information > Initial set time (p.2).
2.4 Characteristics stated by the manufacturer.
    - Ideal for filling, setting, plugging and patching
    - Very rapid hardening, strong and easy to use
    - High early strength
    - Fast setting
2.5 Compressive strength.
    | Time | Compressive strength |
    | 1 hour | ~ 5 MPa |
    | 24 hours | ~ 7 MPa |
    | 28 days | ~ 15 MPa |
    Test method printed: (AS 1478.2:2005)
2.6 Packaging, shelf life and storage.
    - Packaging: 8 kg pail
    - Shelf life: 6 months
    - Storage conditions: Product must be stored in original, unopened and undamaged sealed packaging in dry conditions at temperatures between 4 °C and 35 °C.

3 SUBSTRATE PREPARATION
3.1 General. Prepare substrates in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (May 2026, Version 01.01) and the requirements below. Inspect the substrate against these requirements before application.
3.2 Substrate preparation.
    - All surfaces must be clean, sound and free from dust, ice, oils, grease or other surface contaminants such as curing membranes and form release agent etc.
    - Bolt holes and fixing pockets should be free of dirt and debris by air blasting. For maximum bond, surfaces should be abraded or roughened, preferably by mechanical means such as needle gun, grit blasting, grinding etc. All prepared surfaces must be saturated with water several hours prior to grouting, ensuring it is free of any surface water or puddles

4 APPLICATION
4.1 General. Apply in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (May 2026, Version 01.01) and the requirements below.
4.2 Application data.
    - Mixing ratio: 960–1,120 mL of clean potable water for 8 kg
    - Yield: ~ 3.6 litres per 8 kg
    - Layer thickness: 5 mm - 100 mm
    - Initial set time: ~ 5 minutes at 23 °C / 50 % r.h. (AS/NZS 2350.4-2006)
    - Final set time: ~ 20 minutes at 23 °C / 50 % r.h (AS/NZS 2350.4-2006)
4.3 Mixing.
    - The water addition should be 12–14 % of the dry weight of the product or sufficient to make a usable consistency.
    - Measure the right amount of clean, potable water 960–1,120 mL of water to a 8 kg bucket of Davco® Jetcrete.
    - To mix the product, add the water and roll the bucket on the ground with occasional vigourous shaking for 1 minute. Hand mix the final product for complete mixing.
    - Continue to mix until a creamy consistency is achieved, free of lumps of powder.
    - Use within 5 minutes of mixing. The product may set faster in hot conditions.
    - Do not mix with ordinary portland cement as immediate setting may occur.
    - If required use a small amount of additional water to achieve the desired consistency.
    - Thoroughly dampen the existing concrete before placing Davco® Jetcrete.
4.4 Curing treatment. The products will develop its highest strength when cured for a minimum of 24 hours after placing with one of the following methods:
    - Polythene sheeting
    - Water curing, such as mist spraying
    - Wax or resin-based compound
    Note: Setting time is affected by site conditions, climate and could be faster or slower than specified.
4.5 Limitations and important considerations.
    - Davco® Jetcrete must not be applied at elevated temperatures above 30 °C or in hot windy conditions.
    - Davco® Jetcrete should be protected from rain and frost for the first 24 hours.
    - Allow Davco® Jetcrete to set firmly before return to service.

5 QUALITY CONTROL AND TESTING
5.1 Hold point. Before each application, measure and record the conditions in clause 5.2 and compare them with the manufacturer's limits. HOLD POINT: do not proceed until the Superintendent has released the hold point.
5.2 Conditions stated in the limitations. Also stated in the data sheet limitations (clause 4.5):
    - Davco® Jetcrete must not be applied at elevated temperatures above 30 °C or in hot windy conditions.
    - Davco® Jetcrete should be protected from rain and frost for the first 24 hours.
5.3 Test methods printed beside stated values. Each value is as printed in the data sheet with its test method.
    - Compressive strength: Time | Compressive strength; 1 hour | ~ 5 MPa; 24 hours | ~ 7 MPa; 28 days | ~ 15 MPa (AS 1478.2:2005)
    - Initial set time: ~ 5 minutes at 23 °C / 50 % r.h. (AS/NZS 2350.4-2006)
    - Final set time: ~ 20 minutes at 23 °C / 50 % r.h (AS/NZS 2350.4-2006)
5.4 Basis of the stated values. All technical data stated in this Product Data Sheet are based on laboratory tests. Actual measured data may vary due to circumstances beyond our control.
5.5 Other tests. For any test method, sampling frequency or acceptance criterion not stated in this clause: refer to manufacturer and the project specification.

6 WARRANTY AND DOCUMENTATION
6.1 Documents to be obtained and submitted. Obtain the current issue of each document before ordering and submit it with the product submission. Documents are listed as published on the manufacturer's website.
    - Product Data Sheet: Davco® Jetcrete, May 2026, Version 01.01, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/e/davco-jetcrete.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: Davco Jetcrete, version 09/04/2025, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/g/MSDS%20Davco%20Jetcrete%20GHS7.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: SDS Various Semi-Finished, version 11/05/2026, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/a/sds-various-semi-finished-1.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: SDS Davco Jetcrete, version 11/05/2026, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/c/sds-davco-jetcrete.pdf
6.2 Ecology, health and safety. For information and advice on the safe handling, storage and disposal of chemical products, users shall refer to the most recent Safety Data Sheet (SDS) containing physical, ecological, toxicological and other safety-related data.
6.3 Warranty. Obtain any product or installation warranty in writing from the manufacturer or its authorised applicator and file it with the project records. Warranty terms: refer to manufacturer.
    - Legal notes: In practice, the differences in materials, substrates and actual site conditions are such that no warranty in respect of merchantability or of fitness for a particular purpose, nor any liability arising out of any legal relationship whatsoever, can be inferred either from this information, or from any written recommendations, or from any other advice offered.
6.4 Application records. Record the product name, batch numbers, dates, areas treated and the conditions measured under clause 5.2, and include the records in the project documentation.
